name: Should I expand the bathroom or add a second bathroom instead?

mainEntity.name: Is it better to make one bathroom larger or use the money to add another bathroom?
mainEntity.text: Is it better to make one bathroom larger or use the money to add another bathroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether to expand one bathroom or add another depends on how the home is used. If the house has one cramped bathroom serving multiple bedrooms, a second bathroom may improve daily function and resale value more than making the existing bath larger. If the home already has enough bathrooms and the goal is comfort, a larger primary bath can be the better investment. In Los Angeles-area homes, space constraints often make both options challenging, so the decision should be based on traffic flow, bedroom count, and the most likely buyer profile. Adding another bathroom can create stronger utility, but it may also require more plumbing, electrical, and structural work. Expanding one bathroom can deliver a higher-end feel with less complexity if the existing footprint is already close to workable. The right choice usually comes from comparing two or three concept plans and estimating both cost and long-term use. A designer or builder should help weigh convenience, resale, and construction difficulty before a final decision is made.
acceptedAnswer.description: The better choice depends on the home’s layout, resale goals, and how many bedrooms share the bathroom. In many homes, adding a second bathroom helps daily function more than enlarging one existing bathroom, but a larger primary bath can be better for luxury and comfort.
